name: Dodge / SRT Viper 8.4 L V10 (Gen V, 2013-2017; notes give the 2008-2010 Gen IV figures)
summary: A 90-degree pushrod V10 with two rods on each of five crank pins, so it cannot fire evenly: the gaps alternate long and short instead of a steady 72 degrees. That lumpy, off-beat pulse train at low revs (6,200 rpm redline) through side exhausts is the Viper sound.

rod_length_mm.note: 'Forged, powder-metal connecting rods measuring 158.6 mm'. The release does not say centre-to-centre, but that is the usual meaning (158.6 mm = 6.244 in).

displacement_cc.note: Wikipedia and supercars.net; pi/4 x 103^2 x 100.6 x 10 = 8,382 cc (my check).

firing_order.note: Numbering per the same page: odd cylinders 1-3-5-7-9 on the left bank (bank 1), even 2-4-6-8-10 on the right bank, cylinder 1 at the front left. Source is rerev.com, a firing-order reference site, not a Chrysler document; I could not open a factory manual or the Viper Club pages (HTTP 403).

crank.value: Forged steel, six main journals. Two connecting rods per crank pin; the pins are not split, which is why a 90-degree V10 fires unevenly.
crank.note: Six mains and forged steel are from the Stellantis release. The shared (unsplit) pins are NOT stated on any Chrysler page I opened: en.wikipedia's V10 engine page says only that the Viper is 'a 90-degree engine with odd firing order to obviate the need for a balance shaft', and its Firing order page lists the 1992-2017 Viper V10 among odd-firing engines. Treat the pin layout as a well-supported inference, not a quoted fact.

firing_intervals_deg.note: NOT from a Viper page. Audi states 54/90 for its own 90-degree V10 with shared crank pins (linked source); the same geometry applies to any 90-degree V10 with five shared pins 72 degrees apart. Search-result snippets of Viper Club threads gave the same 54/90 for the Viper but the pages refused to load, so this is unverified at source. My derivation for the order above: the two cylinders on one pin fire 90 degrees apart (10->9, 4->3, 6->5, 8->7, 2->1) and the step to the next pin is 54 degrees (1->10, 9->4, 3->6, 5->8, 7->2); 5 x (90+54) = 720.

valves_per_cylinder.note: 20 valves; roller hydraulic lifters, pushrods. Valves angled 12 degrees. Combustion chamber 72 cc.

intake_lift_mm.note: Not found for the 8.4. A search snippet quoted a factory manual figure of 0.541 in lift with 297/305 degrees duration for the 1997 8.0 L engine; page not opened, different engine, not used.

exhaust_duration_deg.note: Not found. Exhaust lobes are phased independently of the intake by the cam-in-cam VVT; range not found.

redline_rpm.note: 'Maximum engine speed (redline) is 6,200 rpm with fuel cutoff at 6,400 rpm.' supercars.net lists 6,250 rpm for the 2008 car.

peak_power_kw.note: 640 hp per the release, converted by me (x 0.7457). 2008-2010 engine: 600 hp (447 kW) at 6,100 rpm (supercars.net, Stellantis 2007 release).

peak_power_rpm.note: The Stellantis release gives no rpm; Wikipedia cites supercars.net.

peak_torque_nm.note: 600 lb-ft per the release, converted by me (x 1.3558). 2008-2010 engine: 560 lb-ft (759 N·m) at 5,000 rpm.

intake_type.value: plenum: composite intake manifold with two electronic throttle bodies
intake_type.note: 2013: composite manifold with runners 'approximately one inch longer than the previous design'. 2008: two-piece cast aluminium manifold fed through 'dual electronic throttle control modules' (https://media.stellantisnorthamerica.com/print.do?id=7402).

runner_length_mm.note: Not found; only the relative statement above.

header_type.value: stainless tube-in-shell headers with individual runners per cylinder, one per bank; collector layout not stated
header_type.note: 2008 release calls them 'tubular air-gap headers' with individual stainless runners.

exhaust_notes.value: Catalysts close to the headers; the Viper's exhausts exit through the sills (side exhaust) on these generations.
exhaust_notes.note: 2013 SRT brochure lists 'Exhaust system - dual-side sport' and sill-mounted exhaust. Whether there is a crossover between banks was not found.

header primary dimensions and whether the banks are crossed over

sources.what: Chrysler Group (now Stellantis) press release on the 2013 SRT Viper V10. Manufacturer; bore, stroke, rod length, valve sizes, compression, redline.
Chrysler press release for the 2008 Dodge Viper SRT10 (first 8.4). Manufacturer; intake, heads, VVT description.
supercars.net page for the 2008 Viper SRT-10: reproduces the Chrysler release plus a spec table.
English Wikipedia Viper engine page; displacement and peak rpm figures.
rerev.com firing-order page for the Dodge 8.4 L; automotive reference site, not a factory source.
English Wikipedia V10 engine page; states the Viper is a 90-degree odd-firing engine.
English Wikipedia Firing order page; lists the Viper V10 among odd-firing engines.
Audi MediaCenter engine text for the R8 V10; used only as the stated 54/90 interval for a 90-degree shared-pin V10.

curb_kg.note: 'Curb Weight, lb. (kg) 3,354 (1,521.4) – Viper model; 3,297 (1,495.5) – Viper model with SRT Track Package; 3,431 (1,556.3) – Viper GTS model'.

gear_count.note: 'TRANSMISSION: MANUAL SIX-SPEED OVERDRIVE'; the engine release names it the 'Tremec TR6060 six-speed manual transmission' (https://media.stellantisnorthamerica.com/newsrelease.do?id=12199).

final_drive.note: 'Axle Ratio 3.55', 'Overall Top-gear 2.24'. Release: 'the final-drive ratio has been shortened to 3.55 from 3.07' (https://media.stellantisnorthamerica.com/newsrelease.do?id=12199).

wheel_radius_m.note: Rear tyre 'Revs per Mile (rpm) 764'; radius = 1609.344 m / 764 / 2 pi, my conversion.

tyre.note: 'Rear Standard Size and Type P355/30ZR19, Pirelli P Zero'; front 295/30ZR18. Rear-wheel drive.

top_speed_kmh.note: 'Top speed = 206 mph', converted by me (331.5 km/h).

driven.note: English Wikipedia, 'Dodge Viper' (read 2026-11-17), infobox layout: Front mid-engine, rear-wheel-drive.
